articles.title: CF Montreal are for sale: What it means, how much it could cost, and what’s next for the MLS club
articles.summary: In an emotional press conference, CF Montreal’s founder and owner Joey Saputo refused to rule out relocation. In a rare press conference, CF Montreal owner Joey Saputo announced that his family was beginning the process of “initiating a structured sale process” of the MLS club.
body: “This decision is neither driven by urgency, nor dictated by circumstance,” Saputo said in his initial scripted remarks. “It’s the result of a careful and deliberate reflection on where we stand today, and more importantly, on the opportunities that lie ahead for the club.”

Throughout his statement, Saputo stressed his desire to keep the club in Montreal, saying he hoped to find someone who “shares commitment to Montreal and who will ensure that the club remains in the city for many years to come.”
Yet, more than half an hour into the event after the floor was open for in-person questions, Saputo refused to rule out selling to a buyer who might move the club.

“I will not discount the club to the point of just giving it away just for the sake of giving it away,” Saputo said. “I want to be perfectly clear. I love this club. I will love this club to stay here. But if an owner comes in that doesn’t have the capacity to keep the club at the level that it needs to be at, and to spend the money that needs to be spent in order to bring in the players that this city wants to see, then at that point I’m not doing anyone a favor by selling it to someone just to keep it here.

articles.title: Carrick position increasingly in doubt as hierarchy mulls over his future
articles.summary: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, but Sky Sports News has been told as yet, no final decision has been taken about his future.
body: As reported earlier on Monday, the club is carrying out a full review of the team's performance so far this season, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, with a plan for a decision to be made before the end of this international break.
Carrick was given a reprieve following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago, with the bosses keen to give him a further three matches to try to turn the team's fortunes around.

But the pressure has continued to mount on Carrick after an eighth straight Premier League match without a win. There are now real doubts about whether he will be in charge of the team which goes to Anfield to play Liverpool the weekend after next.
The United hierarchy is determined that results have to improve, but they want to be sure about which direction to take the team before any action is taken.

articles.title: Michael Carrick facing Manchester United axe amid review by Jason Wilcox
articles.summary: Director of football in discussions with Omar Berrada. Pochettino and Howe on radar as possible replacements. Manchester United are moving towards sacking Michael Carrick, though no final decision has been made by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, who is leading the review after the head…
body: Wilcox has been consulting with Omar Berrada, the chief executive, before a recommendation regarding Carrick is made to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy.

If Carrick is removed, Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a potential candidate as it is understood the USA head coach is open to the position, while sources indicate that Eddie Howe also remains on the radar of Wilcox too.

The former Newcastle manager is taking a break from the game but would consider the job if offered it. United are in the Premier League relegation zone and have three victories in 15 games in all competitions. Carrick came close to being removed after the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October. But after Wilcox and Berrada met the following day at the training ground to discuss his position, Carrick was given the three games until the international break to prove he and the players could reverse a dismal start.

A defeat, a win and a draw in those matches plus the team’s displays in each compounded with the overall run of form has moved Wilcox and Berrada towards a position where they are minded to remove Carrick. There is a growing expectation within the club that he will lose his job.

articles.title: Manchester’s soulless content machine football clubs sum up post-imperial Britain | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: United and City dominate the news cycle with stories so strange and vast they threaten to consume the rest of the league. In Manchester this weekend it was possible to bookend your Thursday‑to‑Sunday entertainment with two cultural events.
body: As expected, one of these events provided a visceral cinematic experience, a deeply disturbing two-hour public meditation on the meaning of faith, blood, fear, power, ritual and the fetishising of objects, climaxing in an orgiastic crowd scene of depraved but undeniably erotic abandon, all acted out on a set in a state of glorious and performative ruin. And the other one was a film with Oliver Reed in it.

By the final whistle that wild 4‑4 draw at Old Trafford felt like a fitting endpoint to the opening quarter of the Premier League season. As we head into a 12‑day international break it is customary at this point to take a set of readings, to anatomise the season to date, to offer up a state of the Premier League address.

articles.title: NI's O'Neill ruled out of Nations League matches
articles.summary: Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill is ruled out of Northern Ireland's final two Nations League fixtures against Ukraine in Belfast and Hungary in Budapest.
body: Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill has withdrawn from the Northern Ireland squad for the forthcoming Nations League matches against Ukraine and Hungary because of injury.
O'Neill won his first senior cap against Guinea in June and came on as a late substitute in the Nations League wins over Georgia and Ukraine in the last international window.

The 18-year-old, who now has four international caps, recently made his first senior appearance for Arsenal, starting in the Carabao Cup last-16 tie against Fleetwood Town, which the Gunners lost in a penalty shootout.
O'Neill joins Sunderland defender Dan Ballard, Eoin Toal, and midfielders Ali McCann and Jamie McDonnell in being ruled out of the upcoming double-header because of injury.

articles.title: Birmingham announce shock Brady departure
articles.summary: Birmingham have announced the shock departure of NFL legend Tom Brady as minority owner with the Bluenoses sitting top of the Championship table.
body: In a statement, the club said: "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

"It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community."

Brady, a seven-time Super Bowl champion in his playing days, bought a minority stake in the club in August 2023 during its takeover by an American capital management firm but saw the club relegated in his first season after the surprise sacking of John Eustace.

A summer of considerable spending, including the third-tier record £15m signing of England U21 forward Jay Stansfield, saw them promoted back to the Championship at the first time of asking before the club recorded a 10th-placed finish on their first season back in the second tier.

articles.title: Sabalenka starts pursuit of WTA Finals title with opening win
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka got off to a winning start at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, battling past Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5 in the opening match in Group 2 on Monday.
body: A two-time beaten finalist in the WTA Finals - including going down last year to Elena Rybakina, who stole her No 1 ranking this season - Sabalenka is looking to win the tournament for the first time.

Rybakina's late withdrawal due to a viral illness and fatigue aids Sabalenka's hopes, as does her opening victory over Wimbledon finalist Muchova, who made her sweat for it in a hugely-absorbing contest that ran six minutes shy of two hours.

Sabalenka was first to blink on serve in the first set, Muchova breaking for a 3-2 advantage, and again to lead 5-4, only for her opponent to break back immediately on both occasions - the second time when the Czech world No 7 was serving to take the opener.
Sabalenka then spurned a couple of set points in Muchova's next service game, but dominated the resulting tiebreaker, dropping just two points.

articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama's love for San Antonio is officially one of a kind. Literally. The Spurs superstar is turning heads in the trading card world after Topps shared a look at an ultra-rare, one-of-one autographed card with a handwritten message for the Alamo City.
body: Next to his signature, in bright blue ink, are the words: "I ♥ SATX."

The card, part of Topps' Five Star collection, features Wembanyama in his Spurs jersey, surrounded by elaborate gold detailing and a bold blue autograph. A "1/1" marking at the bottom confirms it's the only one.
For Spurs fans, the personal touch might be just as meaningful as the signature itself.

Collectors prize one-of-one cards, especially those with an autograph from a star. Wembanyama has become a hot commodity since the Spurs selected him No. 1 overall in the 2023 NBA Draft, with his rare cards drawing considerable attention.

articles.title: Shocking 49ers-Raiders fan brawls a sad reminder of sports' ugly underbelly
articles.summary: Days after the Bay Area celebrated a feel-good, unifying event - the Golden State Valkyries parade - mayhem at Sunday's 49ers-Raiders game reminded us how unique that vibe really is in sports.
body: Four days after the Bay Area celebrated a love-infused, feel-good, unifying sports event - the Golden State Valkyries championship parade - we were sadly reminded of just how unique and rare that vibe really is in the sports world.

The San Francisco 49ers and the Las Vegas Raiders got together to show us all the worst, nastiest underbelly of the shared sports experience. Sunday's 49ers-Raiders game could be remembered for a lot of things. The 49ers' improvement to 7-1, their best start since 2019. Perhaps Kirk Cousins' last game as a Raider, with the trade deadline looming Tuesday.
Instead it will likely be remembered for the fights and violence captured on video both inside Levi's Stadium and outside in the parking lot.

The video that truly went viral was recorded by content creator FriscoPhillyB (frisco_phillyb4x on Instagram) in the main parking lot outside of Levi's. It shows Raiders and 49ers fans viciously punching each other and slamming each other into the parking lot concrete, with at least two of the participants unconscious. The video began circulating Sunday night and by Monday morning it had been aggregated everywhere, with over a million views.
points: Days after the Bay Area celebrated a feel-good, unifying event - the Golden State Valkyries parade - mayhem at Sunday's 49ers-Raiders game reminded us how unique that vibe really is in sports.

Pochettino signed a four-year contract extension with the U.S. men's national team in August, following a round of 16 finish at the 2026 FIFA World Cup in Canada, Mexico and the United States. Prior to taking over the USMNT in 2024, Pochettino held several high-profile managerial positions in Europe, including in the Premier League with Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea F.C.
The U.S. men's national team will play in the quarterfinals of the Concacaf Nations League on Nov. 14 and 17 against Haiti. Both matches will be played in the United States.
